chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hakam ibn Jumhur, from his father, he raised it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade Nikah al-Shighar, which is al-Mumatahah, and it is when a man says to another man: 'Marry me to your daughter so that I may marry you to my daughter, on the condition that there is no dowry between us.'
The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Marriage is valid on what is permissible to possess, such as wine and pork.
ai.seo_question: What is Nikah al-Shighar and is it valid in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith defines *Nikah al-Shighar* as an exchange of daughters where no dowry (*mahr*) is paid to either side, a practice explicitly prohibited by the Prophet. Sheikh al-Tusi clarifies the juristic nuance that while the daughters themselves are permissible to possess, the validity of this specific marriage structure is distinct from prohibitions based on the nature of the exchanged commodity, such as wine or pork, which are invalid due to their inherent impurity.
